### `expect.getState()`

Returns the current state of the `expect` module. This is useful for accessing test metadata inside `beforeEach`, `afterEach`, custom matchers, or any code that runs during a test.

These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).
